newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAfrica 1996 gold output 494.62 tonnes, 40-yr low.
newsitem.headline: SAfrica 1996 gold output 494.62 tonnes, 40-yr low.

text.p: South Africa's gold production dropped to 494.62 tonnes in 1996 from 522.38 in 1995, the Chamber of Mines said on Monday.
The industry's output last year was the lowest since 1956 when the country's gold mines produced 494.44 tonnes of the yellow metal.
South African gold output has been declining steadily with rising working costs and dwindling grades chipping away at production in the country -- the world's largest gold producer.
The chamber said 1996 gold output was 5.3 percent lower than the previous year.

"It is estimated that the decline in production of 27.8 tonnes is equivalent to a loss of revenue to the industry and foreign exchange to South Africa to the order of 1.5 billion rand," the chamber said in a statement.
It said reasons for the drop in production included; workplace disruptions, ongoing consolidation in the industry, escalating costs and a focus on quality mining at the expense of tonnage.
Chamber figures show that gold output rose in December to 43,994.1 kilograms from November's 41,680.7.
